## Overview

Adds an opt-in, per-request output for generation: a model that implements `SupportsAuxReadout` declares named float32
readouts (for example an N-way decision head). They are computed from the hidden-state rows that `compute_logits`
reads, only for requests that set `SamplingParams.aux_readouts`, and are returned in `CompletionOutput.aux_readouts`.
The engine must be started with `--enable-aux-readouts`; without it, nothing changes.

First PR of RFC #62145. It is the stateless part only: no intermediate-layer capture, no branch with its own KV/GDN
state, and no Decisions API change.

## Claims

- **New output.** Row `i` of `aux_readouts[name]` is the readout computed from the hidden state that the logits of
  generated token `i` were computed from. It is a float32 CPU tensor `[len(token_ids), width]`, returned with the
  final output. `output_kind=DELTA` is rejected, because a DELTA final output carries only its last tokens.
- **Off by default, no work unless asked.**
  - With the flag off, the runner holds no readout state, and requests that set `aux_readouts` are rejected.
  - With the flag on, a step in which no scheduled request asked does no readout work.
  - Requests that did not ask get `None`.
- **No change to generation.**
  - Readouts are computed after the forward, next to `compute_logits`; CUDA graph dispatch is untouched.
  - No host synchronization is added. This was checked with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, including a negative
    control (see Validation).
- **Small.** 246 added and 2 changed library lines (docstrings included) across 13 files, following the path
  that `prompt_token_id_logprobs_dict` already takes. Model Runner V2 only. The engine refuses at start-up with
  speculative decoding, tensor, pipeline or context parallelism.
- **Checked model contract.** A head that returns anything other than `[rows, sum(aux_readout_dims)]` raises a
  `ValueError` naming the model and the expected shape; this check reads tensor metadata only.

## Validation

All runs used one B200, on the base commit of this branch (`da9134b`), with the PR files overlaid. There was no
nightly image for that commit, so the environment was assembled and checked as follows:

- compiled extensions from the per-commit wheel of `f98ae6a`, an ancestor of `da9134b` with no change to `csrc/`,
  `cmake/`, `CMakeLists.txt` or `requirements/` in between (the engine log reports `0.32.0rc1.dev342+gf98ae6a9f`);
- every file under `vllm/` replaced by the `da9134b` source and re-hashed: 3,389 files, 0 mismatches;
- Python dependencies from the `nightly-39983a5` image (requirements unchanged between `39983a5` and `da9134b`).

The Rust frontend extension is not part of this environment; none of the tests below use it. The same code was also
run on the `39983a5` nightly image with the same results.

**Tests**

| What | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New tests, 4 runs | `pytest -v tests/v1/sample/test_aux_readouts.py tests/v1/sample/test_aux_readout_params.py`, once plain and 3× with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 24 passed in each of the 4 runs |
| Sync-check control | a head that calls `float(t.sum())` on a GPU tensor, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | the request fails with `GPU<->CPU sync detected`; the same head without the sync passes |
| Existing tests, before and after the change | `pytest tests/test_sampling_params.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/models/test_registry.py` | no new failures: 701 passed before and after; the same 10 failed and 34 errors (same tests) also occur on this base without the change |
| mypy on the 13 changed files | `mypy --follow-imports=silent <files>` | no new errors: 28 before and 28 after, the same errors apart from line numbers |
| Lint | `ruff check` / `ruff format` (v0.14.0) | clean |

The new tests live under `tests/v1/sample`, so the existing "V1 Sample" CI job (H200 MIG 18GB) runs them. Each
of the two engines they start uses `gpu_memory_utilization=0.3`.

What the new GPU tests check, on `facebook/opt-125m` with a test-local 3-way head made of three rows of the output
embedding:

- the readout equals the engine's own raw logits of those three tokens (`logprob_token_ids`) at every generated
  token;
- the head runs only for rows that asked;
- requests that ask and requests that don't, in one batch, generate the same tokens and logprobs as when nobody asks;
- a request that hits the prefix cache still gets the correct readout;
- a prompt prefilled over several steps (step budget 32 tokens) gets one correct row per generated token;
- an aborted request leaves no readout state behind;
- with the feature on but unused, generation matches an engine started without the flag;
- invalid names, `output_kind=DELTA`, and requests to an engine without the flag, are rejected.

CPU unit tests also call the runner's readout step directly: it gathers exactly the `logits_indices` rows of the
asking requests, skips requests with no logits rows without calling the head, and raises on a wrong head shape. The
start-up refusals (tensor, pipeline, context parallelism) are tested the same way.

**Real hybrid architecture** (out of tree): a random-weight 8-layer Qwen3.5 with GDN and full-attention layers, and a
stateless 3-way head on the final hidden state.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Readout vs the engine's label logits | max \|Δ\| 8.6e-4, 0 argmax flips |
| Generation when some requests ask vs when none ask, same batch | 0/8 sequences differ, logprob gap 0 (2 runs) |
| Readout rows computed | 0 with no asking request, 8 with 8 asking requests |
| Generation, feature on but unused, vs an engine without the flag (GDN state dtype set to float32 on both) | 0/8 sequences differ, logprob gap 0 (2 runs; stock vs stock 0/8) |

## Details

**Why this is not duplicate work.**
- #59543 (open) returns the raw last hidden state per generated token to the client.
- This PR returns a model-defined head's few floats from the same rows, through the same kind of path.
- If #59543 lands first, this change can share its runner gather and transport, leaving only the
  `SupportsAuxReadout` call. RFC #62145 asks whether the two should be one channel.
- The existing `aux_output_connector` (routed experts) is built for per-token captures keyed by KV block hashes, with
  its own store. A few floats at the sampled rows do not need that machinery, so this PR does not use it.

**Design.**
- `SupportsAuxReadout` has two members: `aux_readout_dims` (name → width) and
  `compute_aux_readouts(hidden_states) -> [num_rows, total_width]`. Widths are recorded in `_ModelInfo`, so the
  frontend can validate names without loading the model.
- In `sample_tokens`, the runner gathers the asking requests' rows by the same `logits_indices` that `sample()` used.
  It calls the model once per step and splits the result per request into `ModelRunnerOutput.aux_readouts`.
- `AsyncOutput` copies the readouts to the host on the output copy stream.
- The scheduler cuts each request's rows to its kept tokens, into `EngineCoreOutput.new_aux_readouts`, appended last.
- The output processor concatenates the rows on finish and slices them by name.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- Readouts are returned with the final output only, and only through the Python API (no OpenAI-compatible field yet).
- Not supported yet: speculative decoding, tensor, pipeline and context parallelism. They are refused at
  start-up. Tensor parallelism is refused because it was not validated and a head may read TP-sharded weights
  (the test head reads rows of `lm_head`).
- During chunked prefill, the row of a chunk that does not finish the prompt is computed and discarded, like its
  logits (Model Runner V2 computes one logits row per scheduled request).
- Readouts follow the precision of the hidden state. Across a prefix-cache hit they match the engine's logits for that
  request, not bit-for-bit the readout of an uncached run.
- Not covered by this change, but met while validating it: a model that subclasses an existing architecture and is
  registered under a new name does not get that architecture's name-keyed config adjustments (`MODELS_CONFIG_MAP`).
  For Qwen3.5 the GDN state dtype then resolves to `auto`, and in our hybrid check 2 of 8 sequences differ from
  stock (logprob gap 0.0078). That stock resolves to float32 is read from `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP`, not observed: in our
  matched runs we set float32 explicitly on both sides. With `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32` they match. This happens
  with or without readouts. Should it be documented, or should a subclass inherit its parent's adjustments?
- Tested on NVIDIA only. The new tests also run in the ROCm mirror of "V1 Sample", which we could not run.

**AI assistance** was used to prepare this change (Claude Code); the commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer.
The submitter has reviewed every changed line (library, tests and docs) and the validation above.

@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+# Auxiliary Readouts
+
+A model can declare *auxiliary readouts*: small float32 outputs, such as an
+N-way decision head, computed from the same hidden states that generation
+samples from. A request asks for them by name, and they come back with its
+completion. Other requests in the same batch are not affected, and no readout
+work is done when no scheduled request asks. Model Runner V2 only.
+
+## Model side
+
+Implement `SupportsAuxReadout`:
+
+```python
+class MyModelWithHead(MyModelForCausalLM):
+    supports_aux_readout = True
+    aux_readout_dims = {"decision": 3}
+
+    def compute_aux_readouts(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # hidden_states: [num_rows, hidden_size], the rows compute_logits reads
+        return self.decision_head(hidden_states).float()  # [num_rows, 3]
+```
+
+`compute_aux_readouts` returns all declared readouts concatenated in the order
+of `aux_readout_dims`, as one `[num_rows, sum(aux_readout_dims.values())]`
+tensor; any other shape is an error. During chunked prefill, the row of a chunk
+that does not finish the prompt is computed and discarded, like its logits.
+
+## Request side
+
+```python
+from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+
+llm = LLM("my-org/my-model-with-head", enable_aux_readouts=True)
+params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, aux_readouts=["decision"])
+completion = llm.generate("...", params)[0].outputs[0]
+completion.aux_readouts["decision"]  # float32 tensor [len(token_ids), 3]
+```
+
+- One row is returned per generated token, at the row its logits were computed
+  from. `max_tokens=1` gives a single decision.
+- Requests without `aux_readouts` get `None`.
+- Without `--enable-aux-readouts`, requests that set `aux_readouts` are
+  rejected and the model runner keeps no readout state.
+- Readouts are returned with the final output only, so
+  `output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA` is rejected.
+- Not supported yet: speculative decoding, tensor, pipeline and context
+  parallelism, and the OpenAI-compatible HTTP responses.

+"""CPU tests of the auxiliary-readout model metadata and request validation."""
+
+import dataclasses
+import json
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import ModelRegistry, SamplingParams
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
+from vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces import supports_aux_readout
+from vllm.model_executor.models.opt import OPTForCausalLM
+from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import _ModelInfo
+from vllm.sampling_params import RequestOutputKind
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+
+
+class _ReadoutA(OPTForCausalLM):
+    supports_aux_readout = True
+    aux_readout_dims = {"decision": 3, "score": 1}
+
+    def compute_aux_readouts(self, hidden_states):
+        return torch.zeros(len(hidden_states), 4)
+
+
+class _ReadoutB(OPTForCausalLM):
+    supports_aux_readout = True
+    aux_readout_dims = {"gate": 2}
+
+    def compute_aux_readouts(self, hidden_states):
+        return torch.zeros(len(hidden_states), 2)
+
+
+def test_model_info_readout_dims():
+    info = _ModelInfo.from_model_cls(_ReadoutA)
+    assert info.aux_readout_dims == (("decision", 3), ("score", 1))
+    # The JSON model-info cache returns tuples as lists; the field must stay
+    # hashable after the round trip.
+    loaded = _ModelInfo(**json.loads(json.dumps(dataclasses.asdict(info))))
+    assert loaded.aux_readout_dims == info.aux_readout_dims
+    hash(loaded.aux_readout_dims)
+    assert _ModelInfo.from_model_cls(OPTForCausalLM).aux_readout_dims == ()
+    assert supports_aux_readout(_ReadoutA)
+    assert not supports_aux_readout(OPTForCausalLM)
+
+
+def test_registry_inspects_in_process_classes():
+    """In-process registration hashes _ModelInfo (lru_cache)."""
+    ModelRegistry.register_model("AuxReadoutTestA", _ReadoutA)
+    ModelRegistry.register_model("AuxReadoutTestA", _ReadoutA)
+    ModelRegistry.register_model("AuxReadoutTestB", _ReadoutB)
+    a = ModelRegistry._try_inspect_model_cls("AuxReadoutTestA")
+    b = ModelRegistry._try_inspect_model_cls("AuxReadoutTestB")
+    assert a is not None and b is not None
+    assert dict(a.aux_readout_dims) == {"decision": 3, "score": 1}
+    assert dict(b.aux_readout_dims) == {"gate": 2}
